2026-11-26: three security fixes were applied to BOTH sides (in-tree src/alienclaw/tools and this package) with identical code, so they are not divergences: (1) dotfile rule: the final component that names something is checked ('.env/', '.env/./' were accepted because basename() was ''), and so is the resolved path's final component (symlink to a dotfile); dot-directories stay allowed; (2) checked host vs connected host: the guard refuses backslash/whitespace/control characters, userinfo, '%' in the host, a second ':' outside brackets, host characters outside [a-z0-9._-] after IDNA, and any URL whose urllib/http.client (host, port) differs from the checked one, and it now RETURNS A CANONICAL URL (lower-case scheme/host, IDNA host, port only if given, no userinfo) instead of the input; covers security-review SR-01 (backslash with requests) and SR-03 (multi-colon port split, %2f/%23); (3) assert_no_symlink gained keyword-only operation='write' (message wording only) so read paths can use it; in-tree file_read now calls it on the unresolved path and opens with O_NOFOLLOW (file_read has no staged counterpart). The ssrf_guard/boundary source_blob values above are the FIXED in-tree blobs (uncommitted when written, so absent at source_commit); the CGNAT divergence is unchanged.

2026-11-26 (review follow-up): assert_no_symlink fails closed when a path component cannot be inspected. Python 3.12's Path.is_symlink() re-raises lstat errors other than ENOENT/ENOTDIR/EBADF/ELOOP (EACCES under an unsearchable directory, e.g. /root/.ssh/id_rsa), so a caller catching only ValueError crashed; any OSError is now ValueError('Path not inspectable on <operation>: "<path>" (<reason>)'). Applied to BOTH sides with identical code and message (a new _is_symlink helper), so it is not a divergence. tests/test_uninspectable_path.py is the guard-level part of the in-tree test/tools/test_boundary_uninspectable_path.py. The in-tree test/tools/test_ssrf_guard_connect_host.py changed only in its tool-level test (output url is the caller's input, the new fetched_url is the canonical URL), which is not ported, so tests/test_connect_host.py is unchanged and only its source_blob was refreshed.

Total deadline (staged only, 2026-11-26; PINNING-SECURITY-REVIEW PR-02, plan gate G4): pinned_urlopen's timeout is now ONE time.monotonic() budget for the resolution, every connect attempt (each gets what is left), TLS, sending (re-armed per 16 KiB), the response head and every read of the returned response, across redirect hops; it raises the new pinning.DeadlineExceededError (a TimeoutError and a urllib.error.URLError, with .phase). Under a deadline the one resolution runs in a daemon thread (getaddrinfo cannot be interrupted), at most 16 at once, abandoned ones included; past the cap a call fails closed. timeout must be None or a positive finite number (ValueError/TypeError). build_pinned_opener and PinnedHTTP(S)Connection gained keyword deadline=None (unchanged per-operation behaviour without it). No in-tree counterpart. Tests: tests/test_deadline.py; tests/test_pinning.py test_timeout_reaches_the_socket / test_default_timeout_is_bounded now expect the remaining budget (<= timeout) instead of timeout itself.

Opt-in redirects (staged only, 2026-11-26; plan gate G5): pinned_urlopen(follow_redirects=0) keeps refusing every 301/302/303/307/308 with the same message; with N in 1..20 each hop is re-validated and re-pinned (its own resolution), https -> http is refused, Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization and a caller-set Host are dropped on a cross-origin hop, 307/308 keep method and body, 301/302/303 become a body-less GET (HEAD stays HEAD), the redirect body is never read, and hops share the total deadline. build_pinned_opener is unchanged (still refuses redirects). Data-driven block list (staged only, 2026-11-26; prepares plan gate G3, no decision change): _ip_is_blocked and _is_loopback_name read the new GENERATED module src/agent_tool_sandbox/_blocklist_data.py (written by ../policy/gen_python.py from ../policy/blocklist.v1.json, the table the TS package reads too) instead of the ipaddress.is_* properties, _CGNAT_NETWORK, _METADATA_IPS and _LOOPBACK_NAMES (all three constants removed). Every range is enumerated explicitly; IPv4-mapped and NAT64 are named matchers (block whole / decode the low 32 bits / defer). _resolve_host_ips unwraps IPv4-mapped answers only while the table's ipv4-mapped matcher is a decode (UNWRAP_IPV4_MAPPED, true today). Zero behaviour change on CPython 3.10.22/3.11.17/3.12.13/3.14.9: all 296 shared-corpus verdicts and messages identical, the parity corpus unchanged, and an old-vs-new differential over ~600k addresses per interpreter agreed everywhere; a raw IPv4-mapped IPv6Address handed straight to _ip_is_blocked still skips CGNAT and WireServer (decode_excludes), as in-tree does. On older unpatched interpreters the table's verdicts now apply instead of that interpreter's ipaddress tables. Tests: tests/test_blocklist_data.py (byte-for-byte drift check of the generated module, no is_* attribute in ssrf_guard.py, profile semantics, schema refusals).

Redirect fixes from the shared redirect corpus (staged only, 2026-11-26; plan gate G5): pinned_urlopen reads a non-ASCII Location's bytes as UTF-8 (U+FFFD for invalid sequences) and percent-encodes non-ASCII in the hop's path, query and fragment, after applying the guard's character rule to the decoded URL (before: UnicodeEncodeError escaped, vector relative-non-ascii-path); a redirect with more than one Location header raises SsrfBlockedError 'Refusing redirect (status N): K Location headers' (before: the first was followed); an empty or blank Location is treated as missing, HTTPError at once (before: the same URL was requested again until the hop cap). Tests: tests/test_redirects.py, vectors/redirect-vectors.json.

Caller IRIs (staged only, 2026-11-26): _validate_fetch_url (so assert_safe_fetch_url, resolve_and_validate and pinned_urlopen) applies the character rule to the URL as given, then percent-encodes as UTF-8 every non-ASCII character after the authority (path, query, fragment; existing %XX and ASCII untouched) BEFORE every other check, so the checks and the returned canonical URL see the ASCII form: 'http://bücher.example/café' -> 'http://xn--bcher-kva.example/caf%C3%A9', as WHATWG new URL() writes it (before: the guard returned the raw path and pinned_urlopen let http.client's UnicodeEncodeError escape). _percent_encode_non_ascii moved from pinning.py into ssrf_guard.py and no longer round-trips through urlsplit/urlunsplit (which dropped an empty '?' or '#'); the redirect path now relies on the guard for the encoding and still applies the character rule itself first. The reference returns non-ASCII unchanged: same decision, different URL, declared in tests/test_parity_in_tree.py (IRI_DIVERGENT_URLS). All shared SSRF and redirect corpus verdicts unchanged. Tests: tests/test_caller_iri.py.

2026-11-26 (in-tree commit 8d66853c, second review pass): assert_no_symlink gained keyword-only root=None. With root set it walks the components of the UNRESOLVED path top-down, skips '..', and lstats a component only if realpath(its directory) is at or below realpath(root) (new helpers _at_or_below and _entries_at_or_below): a symlinked prefix (macOS /tmp -> /private/tmp, a symlinked home, a root spelled through a symlink) is accepted, an in-root symlink is still refused ('Symlink rejected' for the final component, 'Symlink in path rejected' otherwise, 'Path not inspectable' on an lstat error), and nothing outside the root is lstat'ed, so an out-of-boundary path gets only assert_inside_boundary's generic 'Path traversal rejected'. root=None keeps the full walk. Same code and messages on both sides, so not a divergence; the staged copy only adds the return annotation Iterator[Path] on _entries_at_or_below (mypy --strict) and genericised docstrings. boundary.py's and tests/test_uninspectable_path.py's source_blob were refreshed to the 8d66853c blobs. Not ported (no staged file tools): file_read's O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK open, fstat S_ISREG, size from the fd and O_NOFOLLOW dir-fd ancestor walk, file_write's root= call, and test/tools/test_file_read_open_races.py; the README read example now shows the open-side hardening. Tests: tests/test_symlinked_prefix.py and tests/test_outside_generic_refusal.py are guard-level adaptations of the new in-tree tests (the documented call order stands in for file_read/file_write; the ALIENCLAW_HOME case is environment wiring and is not ported; each adds root=None back-compat pins); tests/test_uninspectable_path.py keeps its root=None cases and adds root= cases (outside: generic refusal, inside: fails closed), mirroring the two in-tree assertions that now expect the generic error; tests/test_shared_fs_vectors.py's harness passes root= (and O_NONBLOCK on the read open); tests/test_parity_in_tree.py also compares root= outcomes against the reference, including through a symlinked prefix.

2026-11-26 (third, security review of the in-tree fix set; F1 and F2 applied to BOTH sides with identical code and messages, so not divergences): F1, boundary: a path over 4096 UTF-8 bytes or with more than 256 components ('' and '.' skipped, '..' counted; assert_no_symlink also allows the components of os.path.abspath(root)) is refused before any filesystem call by assert_inside_boundary and assert_no_symlink, 'Path rejected: N bytes is longer than the 4096-byte limit' / 'Path rejected: N components is more than the 256-component limit' (new MAX_PATH_BYTES, MAX_PATH_COMPONENTS, _component_count, _assert_path_bounded); _entries_at_or_below carries the containing directory's real path from step to step (dirname for '..', parent_real/part after an in-root entry passed, realpath() only on an out-of-root step), so the walk is linear; before, realpath() per component made it quadratic (an 8 KB path took ~30 s). F2, ssrf_guard._canonical_url rebuilds only the authority and keeps everything after it exactly as given, so an empty '?' or '#' is no longer dropped. Staged only: pinning._join_location replaces urljoin() for a redirect Location, because urljoin() before Python 3.14 drops an empty '?'/'#' (and for a bare '?' keeps the base query); RFC 3986/WHATWG keep them, as does 3.14. No shared SSRF or redirect corpus vector has an empty '?' or '#', so no verdict or message changed and vectors/generate.py was not re-run. tests/test_property_url_guard.py's 'documented drops' now expect the markers kept. New tests: tests/test_path_length_cap.py (guard-level adaptation of test/tools/test_boundary_path_length_cap.py) and tests/test_empty_query_fragment.py (canonical URL from test/tools/test_ssrf_guard_canonical_params.py, plus _join_location). F3 (file_read bounded read) has no staged counterpart.
